Read-only independent challenge of proposed Claude native->canonical incremental-compaction design. User wants only since latest native compaction incl inside long single turn. Native compact_boundary + following user isCompactSummary contains plaintext; source checkpoint contains native primary JSONL. Canonical created_at_ms/last_changed_at_ms derive RelayEvent.recorded_at_ms; worker writes epoch_millis at mj-worker/src/relay/journal.rs:702, same host clock as Claude native. Proposed cutoff: boundary timestamp, select only contiguous canonical prefix whose created_at_ms and last_changed_at_ms <= boundary timestamp (never discard mutated tool/agent spanning it); require unambiguous preceding raw native-user text anchor matching canonical current-context user and coherent timestamp relation, optionally bridge completion banner. Text accepted prompt timestamp isn't equal native user; canonical accepted before native. Question: is this sufficient, what counterexamples exist (timestamp clock jumps, native restored across workers, canonical aggregation spans compaction)? Need accurate and useful intra-turn cutoff; replaying whole containing user turn is not adequate. Investigate timestamp/projection and known Claude banner flow only, not native checkpoint access (already another child). Return concrete recommended safe cutoff and limitations with decisive file refs. Do not edit or run tests.

I’ll trace how relay timestamps and canonical conversation entries are produced, then check whether the proposed cutoff can safely identify an intra-turn native compaction. I’ll keep this read-only and report counterexamples with file references.

Findings delivered to the parent. The proposed timestamp cutoff cannot guarantee an accurate intra-turn suffix: wall-clock ordering is uncertain, and canonical rows can span the compaction boundary. Exact slicing needs a causal mapping to relay events.

I agree timestamps alone unsafe. Evaluate more useful existing provenance: last pre-boundary Claude tool_use id with matching tool_result BEFORE compact boundary, same id canonical Tool status completed/failed. Canonical ToolCall/Update closes agent streams (session_update.rs:27,100), so this tool provides an exact causal barrier: no post-summary assistant content can be in earlier agent row. Cut at that finalized tool canonical position, preserving any earlier tool whose native result appears after summary (or still missing), and any earlier canonical user not found in native pre-boundary prompt sequence (possible in-flight prompt) or mailbox Message not proven in native prefix. Prefer last pre-boundary finalized tool rather than timestamps; retain events between tool and compaction harmless overlap. Check actual ACP Claude ID mapping and ordering, identify counterexamples and minimum checks. Native implementation child working parser/plumbing but cutoff unsettled. Read-only quick design response.

I’ll check whether Claude tool IDs survive the ACP bridge unchanged and whether a completed canonical tool row really marks a safe point in relay order. I’ll report the minimum checks needed for the cutoff and any cases that still require retaining extra context.

A matched, finalized Claude tool result can anchor the cutoff, but the canonical tool row’s position marks its creation, not its completion. The cutoff needs the matching terminal update’s relay ordinal, verified bridge ID mapping, and retention of earlier prompts, mailbox messages, or tools whose presence in the native prefix is unproven. I sent the counterexamples and checks to the parent.

Settled whole-row approximation, retaining anchor Tool itself: cutoff anchor.creation position-1, so all later raw events and anchor's eventual output retained. Pre-anchor agent rows closed by ToolCall creation, native tool_use before boundary is sufficient for causal barrier, no need completion ordinal if anchor retained. Earlier tools must have unique pre-boundary native tool_result and no postboundary uses/results; any terminal refs/output/unresolved earlier tool or unrepresented user/mailbox/plan is barrier to cutoff. Need current native prompt-sequence matching to avoid dropping unrepresented users (including earlier lineage requiring first native complete handoff). Please provide actual bridge tool id mapping evidence from cached installed @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp 0.99.0 package/source or paired native/canonical fixtures; read-only bounded search, no private content. This is last uncertainty before implementation completion. No need insist on exact suffix; we deliberately replay anchor and spanning rows.

I’ll check the installed bridge package and repository fixtures for the raw Claude tool ID to ACP toolCallId mapping. I’ll keep the search bounded to code and test assets and report only the mapping evidence.

The installed Claude ACP bridge maps ordinary native `tool_use.id` directly to ACP `toolCallId`. One exception matters for the cutoff: a permission request can emit the canonical tool row **before** the native `tool_use` appears. For an anchor based on row creation position, require evidence that the row was first emitted from the streamed tool use; matching IDs alone is insufficient. I sent the source locations to the parent.

Thanks for concrete ID evidence. Eager creation before streamed tool_use is safe for our chosen cutoff BEFORE creation: it closes earlier rows even earlier, and any assistant rows after eager creation have position > cutoff, so retained. It increases overlap but doesn't exclude more. The creation needs be before native compaction, not necessarily after native tool_use; both eager permission and streamed use occur before native result/boundary for paired completed ID. I'll retain this policy. Please independently review finalized generic code now (compaction.rs/tests.rs; native still editing, don't review incomplete native) seeking actual loss, budget, repeated-move regressions. Read-only; no cargo (checkpoint suite running). Distinguish acceptable retained overlap from true dropping post-boundary state. Report concrete issues only with code refs.

You’re right about eager creation: cutting before that row retains more context and does not lose later rows. I’ll review only the finalized generic compaction code and tests, focusing on dropped post-boundary state, budget handling, and repeated moves. I won’t inspect the native parser or run Cargo.

I found one real loss path: on a repeated move, a tool created before the prior handoff and updated afterward keeps its old position, so the generic cutoff can discard its new result. I also flagged that a pasted handoff can be mistaken for a real boundary because detection uses text alone. The findings and file references are with the parent.

Need independent consequential trace now: actual InstallHandoff / prompt context placement. Is generated handoff text ever appended as standalone raw canonical User (our generic extractor assumes) or only hidden context installed as WorkerRelayCommand::InstallPromptContext/InstallHandoff context? Trace cross-harness resume installation -> relay -> next CommandStarted -> canonical User. Point exact symbols/shape. Tests so far manufacture generic handoff bodies; verify live code actually exposes them. Also assess whether old tool row CAN update after handoff under this lifecycle (cross-harness restore old source stopped, new tool IDs may collide); if impossible by lifecycle say decisive refs, if possible provenance freshness needed. Read-only; no tests.

I’ll trace the handoff from cross-harness resume through the worker command and canonical projection, then check whether the old source can still update a tool after that handoff. I’ll use the live path to confirm or revise my earlier finding.

The live path confirms a significant gap: cross-harness resume installs the generated handoff as hidden prompt context, so it never becomes the canonical User row that the generic extractor searches for. The current tests manufacture that row. I also retract my earlier claim about an old tool updating after handoff in a normal move: the source is sealed and stopped before the fresh destination session receives the handoff. I sent the trace and references to the parent.

I’ll review the new durable handoff state and its projection path, then check the generic compaction code for a concrete integration loss or budget regression. I’ll leave the native work in progress alone and won’t run Cargo.

I found a production integration miss: ordinary cross-harness resume installs the marked handoff through a relay request that emits no canonical event. The new projector handles only the event-producing startup command, so it never stores `mj_handoff_state` for the ordinary resume path. A later move therefore cannot reuse that handoff. I sent the exact call chain to the parent.

I’ll verify the corrected install route and journal test, then review the finalized Claude cutoff and archive-to-backend test for concrete loss paths. I won’t run Cargo or touch the files.

The corrected install route now journals and projects the marked handoff, and the verified archive test covers its path into compaction. I found one remaining issue: resume awaits a native archive read of up to 256 MiB before entering its cancellable work, so cancellation can stall until that read and parse finish. I sent the references to the parent.

Native parser checks before/after bounded read, every JSONL read/decode and candidate mapping; deterministic >70KiB BufRead cancel test added. Parent owns final acceptance, controller suite currently compiling. Please no further broad review; quick confirm this closes reported cancellation stall except one bounded selected payload read (256MiB local archive) which is joined before cleanup. No extra new APIs unless concrete missing guarantee.
I’ll check only the new cancellation wrapper and parser checkpoints, including whether cleanup waits for the blocking reader. I won’t broaden the review or run tests.

Yes. Explicit cancellation now stops parsing promptly and joins the blocking task before returning; it can still wait for one bounded payload read and hash. One limit: dropping the whole future cancels the token but does not join the blocking task. I sent that distinction to the parent.
